A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying metasurface depth-imaging work, sharing the optical design, hardware specifications and PSF measurements despite substantial computational revisions and a new title. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original PSF measurements, simulated depth-estimation results, experiments on 28 physical scenes and network ablations in Section 4 and the supplements.

after.justification: V2 reports original simulated evaluations across four datasets, experiments on 42 physical scenes and component ablations, alongside retained optical measurements.

M1.justification: V1's explicit PSF-shift extractor and U-Net depth decoder are replaced by fine-tuning DepthAnything V2 on pseudo-RGB inputs containing both polarization channels and their average. V2 also introduces PSF splatting with occlusion/disocclusion handling, polarization-aware augmentation and few-shot real-data adaptation. These substantially change training and inference while retaining the birefringent optical design.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix A adds evaluation using NYU Depth V2's real indoor imagery and MPI Sintel's animated scenes, broadening the represented domains beyond v1's MIT-CGH-4K simulated evaluation and physical object captures. Hypersim training and the earlier general categories of synthetic and physical depth sensing remain.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained DepthAnything V2 and Depth Pro comparisons, v2 evaluates Lotus, Marigold, Metric3D V2, UniDepth V2, ZoeDepth, LiDAR-assisted PromptDA and fine-tuned DepthAnything controls. V1's Intel RealSense D455 comparison and Shen et al. contour-matching comparison are absent from v2's reported evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported working range narrows from 20–150 cm to 20–120 cm, simulated testing changes from 1024×768 processing to native resolutions, and physical evaluation expands from 28 to 42 scenes. V2 introduces held-out Hypersim testing and three backbone sizes. Its metric suite uses L1, RMSE, AbsRel and delta_0.5 instead of v1's AbsRel, delta_1/2/3 and binary accuracy; new PromptDA simulations use downsampled, noisy ground-truth depth.

E4.justification: V1's shift-extraction and centrosymmetric-matching ablations are replaced by tests of polarization prompting, foundation-model initialization, simulator refinement, individual augmentations and one/three/five real training examples (v2 Table 3). V2 Figure 4 adds analysis of simulator boundary and aliasing artifacts. V1's dedicated low-texture failure examples are no longer presented as a failure analysis.

E5.justification: Mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting continues for simulated results, moving from v1 Table 2 to v2's supplementary comparison tables. However, v2's physical results and ablations report point estimates without the variability accompanying v1's physical depth estimates. Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run counts or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V1 reports MIT-CGH-4K AbsRel of 0.13 ± 0.07 and physical AbsRel of 0.21 ± 0.07. V2 reports 0.1023 ± 0.0159 and 0.0594, respectively, for Ours-Base (Tables 8 and 2). These are replacement results under changed methods, ranges and protocols, not controlled version-to-version gains. V2 adds extensive benchmark and ablation results while dropping v1's model-size and binary-accuracy results.

T1.justification: The rotating-PSF relationship and much of its optical derivation are retained, but v2 Appendix E introduces a substantial mathematical rendering model: normalized Gaussian depth distributions, PSF-derived opacity and continuity-dependent compositing. This changes the modeling assumptions beyond simple point-source superposition. The focusing-phase expression also gains the missing -2π/λ factor (v1 Equation 6; v2 Equation 4).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion redefine the central contribution from Nano-3D's custom multi-module depth network to passive nanophotonic prompting of depth foundation models without architectural additions. V2 adds central claims about reducing the simulation-to-real gap and achieving performance comparable to LiDAR-assisted PromptDA, replacing the earlier emphasis on the compact custom network and commercial-camera comparisons.

C2.justification: V2 explains simulator artifacts and domain-transfer mechanisms, and distinguishes ground-truth-aligned baseline geometry from direct metric prediction. It expands v1's planar-label approximation into explicit cautions about nonplanarity, segmentation error and approximate physical scores. Limitations now emphasize restricted field of view, tube length and absent outdoor validation; v1's shift-extractor texture dependence and four-second runtime discussion disappear.

D1.justification: V2 supplies simulator equations and background-extension pseudocode, spectral/depth sampling details, fine-tuning schedules and real-data mixing instructions. It revises the documented fabrication recipe, including o-xylene to amyl acetate development and CHF3/Ar/O2 to BCl3/Ar etching; this establishes changed documentation, not necessarily newly fabricated hardware. V1's promise to release the implementation upon acceptance is absent.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions the work around physically prompting foundation models, contrasting passive optics with LiDAR-based prompting and conventional computational imaging. It adds substantial depth-foundation, prompting, transformer and splatting literature, including PromptDA, while reducing the dedicated fabrication-literature discussion in v1 Section 2.3.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around foundation-model prompting. Related work becomes background plus related work, and the supplements are reorganized into experiments, software and hardware. Optical derivations and implementation material are redistributed, with v1's duplicated implementation discussion consolidated.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns the overview and computational diagrams, adds simulator-artifact illustrations and replaces most result displays with baseline comparison grids and error-map insets. Tables now distinguish fine-tuning, post-alignment and LiDAR assistance through structured columns and color coding. The PSF validation, meta-unit library and fabrication illustrations are retained or reorganized rather than entirely new.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for physical depth cues through matched fine-tuning controls, component ablations and broader domain testing, addressing v1's narrow validation. Simulator analysis and clearer qualifications of physical ground truth also improve scientific accountability. These gains outweigh reduced physical uncertainty reporting and unresolved baseline-score inconsistencies, such as fine-tuned DepthAnything V2's Hypersim L1 of 0.0635 in Table 1 versus 0.0739 in Table 7. The improvement rests on stronger validation and explanation, not direct comparison of errors obtained under changed settings.
